# FAIR-bioHeaders

> FAIR-bioHeaders defines machine-readable provenance headers that travel inside bioinformatics data files: FHR for reference genome FASTA and GFA, FHT for transcriptome FASTA, FHP for protein FASTA, and FHGFF3 for GFF3 annotations. FHGM is a native model-record contract inside FHGFF3, not a fifth file-header type. A header is a block of YAML lines at the top of the file (`;~` in FASTA, `#~` in GFA and GFF3), validated against a JSON Schema and covered by a SHA-512/256 checksum of the file. The reference implementation is the `fair-bioheaders` Python package (command `bioheaders`).

Key facts: FHR/FHP/FHGFF3 retain the v0.6.0 contract set in published fair-bioheaders 0.12.0. FHT v0.7.0 and native FHGM v0.8.0 publication are recorded below; actual final 0.13.0 installed support is pending.

- Schema versions: FHR `schemaVersion: '2.1'`, FHP `'1.2'`, FHGFF3 `'1.2'` (v0.5.0 added top-level `x-` extension fields, FORMAT rule R15; unknown non-`x-` keys stay invalid, nested objects stay closed, and a record that states an earlier minor may not use them; v0.6.0 widened `completeness.lineageDataset` in FHP and FHGFF3 to the dotted BUSCO dataset versions, such as `diptera_odb12.2`, held to records that state `1.2`). A file's `schema` value selects the schema it is validated against; cite a versioned w3id URL. Raw-`main` URLs mean the current schema; an unknown version is reported as unsupported. `fair-bioheaders` 0.11.0 and 0.12.0 bundle the v0.6.0 schemas; 0.10.0 rejects a `…/v0.6.0` citation as an unsupported schema version.
- For supported runtime types, the checksum is computed by `bioheaders combine`, never by hand. Changing any byte except the checksum line invalidates it.
- In FASTA, header values containing `>` or `@` are written as YAML escapes `\x3E` and `\x40` (rule R11), because kseq-based readers start a record at those characters. YAML readers return the real characters.
- Many FASTA tools reject a leading `;` block, including samtools faidx (htslib), pysam `FastaFile`, bedtools getfasta, Picard, Bowtie2, HISAT2, STAR, salmon and Biopython's default `fasta` format. Use `bioheaders strip` to make a plain copy, or `SeqIO.parse(path, "fasta-pearson")` in Biopython. GFF3 and GFA tools surveyed accept `#~` lines.
- A SeqCol digest (`seqcol_id`) is an optional, user-supplied identifier, distinct from the file checksum.

## Specification

- [Format rules R1 to R15](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FORMAT.md): header block placement, checksum coverage, encoding, `>`/`@` escaping
- [Schema versions and selection](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md): versioning policy and how a `schema` URL selects a schema
- [FHP, protein FASTA](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FHP.md): fields, `sourceType`, sources
- [FHGFF3, GFF3 annotation](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FHGFF3.md): header placement after `##gff-version 3`, genome link by checksum or accession plus SeqCol
- [FHGM native model overview](https://fhref.org/specifications/fhgm/): model contract 0.1 was published in shared v0.8.0 at 72cb46b98160ecc7a7f20ef579a6879d5030c40b, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24385999. The published resource is model-contracts/fhgm/0.1/fhgm-model.schema.json. It is selected outside records, adds no FHGM header type/registry row/in-record schema, and has no generated header inventory here. The logical native w3id identifier is pending registration, not a live-link claim. Actual final 0.13.0 runtime acceptance is pending; publication does not establish biology, curator endorsement or JSON-LD.
- [FHR/FHP JSON-LD form](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/JSONLD.md) and [schema.org export](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/SCHEMAORG-EXPORT.md)
- [Tool compatibility](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/TOOL_COMPATIBILITY.md): which tools accept headers, workarounds, upstream support status
- [FAIR header guideline](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/main/docs/FAIR_HEADER_GUIDELINE.md): metadata to put in any file's native header
- [Specification repository](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification): released schemas, LinkML models, examples and conformance vectors

## Schemas

Field-by-field references for each type live on the site, generated from the published
schemas: [FHR](https://fhref.org/specifications/fhr/),
[FHT](https://fhref.org/specifications/fht/),
[FHP](https://fhref.org/specifications/fhp/) and
[FHGFF3](https://fhref.org/specifications/fhgff3/); the overview is
[https://fhref.org/specifications/](https://fhref.org/specifications/).

- [FHR v0.6.0](https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.6.0): reference genome header schema (`fhr.json`)
- [FHP v0.6.0](https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhp/v0.6.0): protein FASTA header schema (`fhp.json`)
- [FHGFF3 v0.6.0](https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhgff3/v0.6.0): GFF3 header schema (`fhgff3.json`)
- FHT: released contract 1.0 in shared v0.7.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24385024. Fixed published schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/v0.7.0/fht.json . Normal form/reference preparation is separate from actual final 0.13.0 installed acceptance and website deployment.

- FHGM: published native model 0.1 in shared v0.8.0, separate from all four file-header contracts. Native identity https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/model-contracts/fhgm/0.1 is a logical identifier pending external alias registration. Retrieve published bytes from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/v0.8.0/model-contracts/fhgm/0.1/fhgm-model.schema.json . No FHGM header schemaVersion, header-registry row, model editor or released-toolkit acceptance is implied.
- [Current FHR schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/main/fhr.json): raw-main canonical URL (also `fhp.json`, `fhgff3.json`)
- [Vocabulary](https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/terms): FAIR-bioHeaders terms (HTML, Turtle or JSON-LD by content negotiation)
- [JSON-LD context v0.6.0](https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.6.0/jsonld/fhr.context.jsonld)

## Tools

- [fair-bioheaders on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/fair-bioheaders/): `pip install fair-bioheaders==0.12.0` (Python 3.9+). Also on [bioconda](https://anaconda.org/bioconda/fair-bioheaders), which has 0.12.0 as checked 2026-11-18.
- [FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools): source, README with every command, container image, Nextflow modules
- [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools/tree/main/plugins/fair-bioheaders): `/plugin marketplace add FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Tools`, then `/plugin install fair-bioheaders@fair-bioheaders`
- [gff3-validator](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/gff3-validator): GFF3 and Sequence Ontology validator ([web app](https://fhref.org/gff3-validator/), `pip install gff3-validator`). Its published 0.1.0 release pins `fair-bioheaders >=0.4,<0.5`, which has no FHGFF3 support, so it reports an FHGFF3 header as not checked (HDR-002) rather than validating it; feature and ontology checking is unaffected.

Common tasks:

```bash
bioheaders combine metadata.yaml genome.fa -o genome.fhr.fa     # add a header (also .gfa, .gff3, protein .faa); computes the checksum
bioheaders verify genome.fhr.fa                                  # validate the metadata and verify the checksum
bioheaders strip genome.fhr.fa genome.fa                         # remove the header; every other byte is kept
bioheaders convert genome.fhr.fa metadata.json                   # also .yaml, .jsonld, .html
bioheaders verify-links annotation.fhgff3.gff3 genome.fhr.fa     # check recorded parent files by checksum
bioheaders assess genome.fa                                      # FAIR checklist for any FASTA, GFF3, GAF, VCF or GFA header (offline)
```

Required fields: all types need `schema`, `schemaVersion`, `taxon` (`name`, `uri` as `https://identifiers.org/taxonomy:<id>`), `version`, `metadataAuthor` and `dateCreated`. FHR adds `genome`, `assemblyAuthor` and `masking`; FHP adds `proteome` and `sourceType`; FHGFF3 adds `annotation` and a genome link (`genomeReference` with `accession` and `seqcol_id`, or a `derivedFrom` item annotating an FHR genome). `checksum` is written by `combine`.

## Independent review and merge authorization (2026-11-18)

Never push directly to the default branch. Use a PR under this authorization.

The maintainer's independent-review rule (2026-11-18) applies only to
FAIR-bioHeaders repositories and agents operated by David Molik (`molikd`) or
Adam Wright (`adamjohnwright`). A PR submitted by either maintainer or their
agents may satisfy the approval gate through an independent **different model**:
Copilot, or a model operated by David or Adam. The approving model/agent must be
other than the submitter; an agent must not self-approve its PR, and another
instance of the same model does not satisfy the different-model requirement.
Record author/reviewer model provenance when needed to establish independence.
David and Adam themselves may self-approve their PRs; this exception does not
apply to their agents.

An eligible agent may merge only after that approval requirement is met, all
applicable CI checks are green, and its own validation of the current changes
passes, including changes after review. Recheck the exact head, base branch,
findings and dependencies immediately before merging. Missing checks are not
passing checks, and branch protection must not be bypassed. Read every overall
review and inline finding, reply with its disposition and fix/evidence, resolve
handled threads, and post an overall response. Merge authorization does not grant
contract adoption, curator acceptance, release, publication or deployment
authority; those retain their separate maintainer gates.

Authority: [approval by another, different model](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/issues/268#issuecomment-6984337685)
and [human self-approval exception](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/issues/268#issuecomment-6984418624).
